description: Patch-level bumps of VersaTiles are automerged here. VersaTiles as this role deploys it is a read-only tile server: the container runs with `--read-only`, its only bind mount is the data directory, and the server never writes to the `.versatiles` container it serves. There is no schema, no migration and no unattended data rewrite that a restart onto a new patch image could trigger, and pinning back to an older version is as reversible as pinning forward.

Nine patch releases of the 4.x line were read before deciding (4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.1.4, 4.1.5, 4.2.1, 4.2.2, 4.6.1, 4.9.1). They are dependency updates, SFTP/HTTP read resilience, memory bounds, and conversion-side work in the `convert` subcommand this role never runs. One of them does touch what the server sends: 4.9.1 changed the MVT content type to `application/vnd.mapbox-vector-tile`, and running 4.8.0 against this scenario confirms it - that version answers the same tile with a bare `vnd.mapbox-vector-tile`. This is precisely why the Molecule scenario asserts the content type rather than a status code. A patch release that changed it again would fail CI and arrive as something a human looks at, instead of silently reaching operators. What automerge would be unsafe for is a harmful change the scenario cannot see; for a read-only tile server the remaining surface of that kind is small and, unlike a data migration, entirely undone by pinning the version back.

The Molecule scenario runs the bumped version and covers what such a bump could plausibly break. It asserts that the running binary reports exactly the `versatiles_version` in defaults/main.yml, that `/tiles/index.json` lists the `osm` source (an instance started without a tile source serves `/` with 200 and the whole front-end, and only gives itself away here), that a tile fetched from `/tiles/osm/0/0/0` is a real Mapbox Vector Tile down to its protobuf framing and shortbread layer names, that the timezone from templates/env.j2 is live in the process, and that the Traefik labels from templates/labels.j2 are attached to the container.

The tile container the scenario serves is a pre-built one downloaded from a pinned release asset, written by a much older VersaTiles in the `versatiles_v02` container format. It is deliberately not generated by the version under test, so the run also proves that the version being merged can still read the files operators already have on disk - the one piece of state a bump here could break.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the tag list sane: ghcr.io/versatiles-org/versatiles-frontend publishes every release four times (`v4.9.1`, `v4.9.1-debian`, `v4.9.1-alpine`, `v4.9.1-scratch`), and strict semver reads the flavoured tags as prereleases and skips them as unstable. `versatiles_container_image_tag` appends the `-debian` flavour itself. The annotation names the `-frontend` image rather than the plain `versatiles` server image because that is the one the role pulls; the two are separate packages that have diverged before (`v3.0.1` was only ever published as a front-end image).
